title: Hierarchical rollout slate with stochastic ramping and auto-rollback
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a flexible rollout configuration and policy engine that supports hierarchical 'slates' of model variants, stochastic (probabilistic) ramping schedules, shadow mirroring with sampling weights, A/B experiment bindings, and automatic rollback driven by multi-dimensional guardrails (latency, error-rate, quality delta on eval prompts). This ticket covers the config schema, policy evaluation loop, runtime hooks for enforcement, and observability surfaces needed for safe production rollouts.

Scope:
- New config schema for a 'rollout slate' that groups variants into tiers (primary, canary, shadow, baseline) and supports per-variant traffic weights, max-step deltas, and oscillation-damping settings.
- Stochastic ramping strategy: allow traffic increases expressed as probability distributions rather than fixed percentages to avoid synchronized bursts across customers.
- Guardrails engine: declarative rules that can reference SLOs (p50/p90 latency), error budget burn, and quality metrics (delta on golden prompt set). Rules support time windows, lookback aggregation, and severity thresholds (soft warn / hard rollback).
- Automatic rollback actions: immediate cutover to baseline, step-back smoothing, or gentle draining depending on severity and configured cooldowns.
- Shadow traffic: configurable sampling rate and request transformation hooks so shadowed requests do not expose customer PII to model telemetry pipelines.
- A/B bindings: first-class support to tie user cohorts to variants with deterministic hashing and cohort size adjustment APIs.
- Observability: new rollout dashboards, per-slate telemetry, and automatic alert wires to SRE/owner channels.

Out of scope: long-term UI work in Console (we will expose the config and a minimal preview API; Console UX refinements are follow-up tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Config schema accepted by platform team and documented (JSON Schema).
Runtime accepts rollout slate JSON and performs traffic shaping with probabilistic ramping in a canary route within 1 hour of deploy in staging.
Guardrail rules can be authored to trigger three actions: warn, soft rollback (reduce traffic by configured delta), hard rollback (full revert to baseline).
Shadowing supports sampling weights and request redaction hooks; shadowed requests are visible in a separate observability stream.
Automated unit + integration test coverage for policy evaluation loop with synthetic metric inputs (latency spikes, quality regression, increased error rate).
End-to-end demo run in staging where a synthetic latency spike triggers a soft rollback, then escalation to hard rollback on continued breach.
decisions: Use a hierarchical 'slate' concept instead of flat variant lists to make policy scoping easier for multi-variant A/B tests and baseline comparisons.
Adopt probabilistic/stochastic ramping as default for initial rollouts to reduce correlated load spikes across tenants.
Guardrail rules are declarative JSON and evaluated in the policy service; enforcement actions are exposed via an idempotent actions API so other services (Router, Autoscaler) can subscribe.
Quality deltas will be computed against a fixed eval prompt set stored in the eval service; the policy engine will only read a pre-aggregated metric to avoid heavy query load.
implementation_notes: Policy engine: new microservice 'rollout-policy' written in Go using our metrics SDK to ingest SLO/bucketed histograms and quality deltas from evals-db.
Router integration: Router will expose an API to accept probabilistic weight updates per route; the rollout-policy service will call Router via signed service token.
Shadowing: implement request copier with a pluggable redaction pipeline (PII rules owned by security).
Fail-safes: policy evaluation runs every 10s with leader election; offline decisions are logged to audit stream and invisible to enforcement until leader reconciles.
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and policy DSL parsing.
Integration test: local simulator that feeds synthetic latency/error/quality metrics and asserts expected action (warn/soft/hard rollback).
Staging E2E: deploy canary slate with two variants and a synthetic traffic generator that causes controlled latency spike; verify observability and rollback actions.
Chaos test: simulated mesh partition to ensure policy leader reconcilation does not cause duplicate rollbacks.
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch and run CI (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ramp-scheduler/pull/612).
Deploy rollout-policy service to staging and point a non-critical route to a rollout slate for validation (staging dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/rollouts/staging/ENG-74109).
Run E2E demo with SRE and PM; adjust default damping parameters as needed.
Canary deploy to production with a single low-traffic customer route for 48h, monitor guardrail signals and manual override cadence.
